items.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025
items.q: I had a lot of fun recording for ECM. ... Manfred Eicher, the producer there, wanted to bring out the best situation... it was actually my cymbal work got amplified on a lot of recordings of ECM because Manfred liked detail.

ctx.x: How about, this is not a person but a record label, ECM? Did you feel that you needed to adjust your style when you played for that —

Not really, because actually it was actually freeing because Manfred Eicher, the producer there, wanted to bring out the best situation, an artistic situation, in music. And it was actually my cymbal work got amplified on a lot of recordings of ECM because Manfred liked detail. And he also liked spontaneity as well as written compositions. And also ECM had a sound that people really liked, and an artistic thing with the covers and it’s still going on today. So it was more about the art of the music rather than…

and they also supported the musicians on their recordings, their touring. So yeah I mean I had a lot of fun recording for ECM. I had my old bands, other good musicians, Keith Jarrett and Gary Peacock’s Standards Trio. So yeah, there was a lot of room to experiment but at a high level of creativity.

items.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Keith sent it to Manfred Eicher... he liked it and he subsequently put it out as Ruta and Daitya... I met Manfred and was asked to do recording because Manfred was interested in recording artists who had played with Miles... Manfred was great. He liked spontaneous improvisations... ctx.x: Oh yeah, if you want to go chronologically we can. Let’s do that, the duet with Keith Jarrett.

OK, well that came about during my tenure with Miles when Keith was in the band. I had a friend of mine, Norman Johnson, whose other friend owned a studio, Poppy Studios, in California, Los Angeles. He gave us three hours of studio time during the day, so we got the electric keyboards brought into the studio, and a nice Steinway Grand. They had some drums in the studio, so I just brought my cymbals. Keith and I had been doing sometimes, on some of the gigs… During the daytime we’d get together and go and…

Manfred Eicher, the producer/director of the world renowned label ECM based in Munich, Germany. Manfred is a producer that produced for classical records. He himself sang in choirs and also played bass in music in different types of settings, free form music and he was familiar with a lot of classical stuff, he honed his recording techniques recording classical music. He had a broad pallet taste for music, but he had an aesthetic for recording music like a movie director. The sessions… He always calls them, still…
